intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding titin (TTN; 188840) on chromosome 2q31.

paragraphs.text: Myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9) is an autosomal dominant myopathy that begins in adulthood. Patients have weakness that may be mainly proximal, distal, or respiratory. Respiratory muscle weakness appears early, often while patients can still walk, and may be the presenting feature (Edstrom et al., 1990; Birchall et al., 2005; Pfeffer et al., 2012). Muscle biopsy shows myofibrillar changes with eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles. Muscle MRI shows selective early involvement of the semitendinosus muscle (Pfeffer et al., 2012; Pfeffer et al., 2014).

paragraphs.text: Edstrom et al. (1990) described 16 patients from 7 pedigrees with an unusual limb-girdle myopathy that began in adulthood. All patients had prominent early weakness of the respiratory muscles. In many, the first neurologic examination was prompted by acute respiratory incapacity. Other early symptoms were neck flexor weakness and sometimes foot extensor weakness. Electrophysiologic studies confirmed a myopathy, and serum muscle enzyme levels were normal or slightly elevated. Muscle biopsies showed myofibrillar changes, including plaques that stained strongly with rhodamine-conjugated phalloidin, a marker for F-actin. On electron microscopy, the plaques consisted of moderately dense thin filaments and were related to splitting of Z discs or extended from Z discs.

paragraphs.text: Chinnery et al. (2001) described a 3-generation family with a novel autosomal dominant myopathy. They clinically assessed 24 family members, 11 of whom were affected. Affected members presented in mid-adult life with weakness of the tibialis anterior, and weakness of the hip and shoulder girdles appeared later in the course. Affected members of the second generation presented earlier, and their disease progressed faster, than those of the first generation. Lung function testing showed progressive global weakness of the respiratory muscles that could be detected from the time of presentation, and in some patients the diaphragm was preferentially involved. Muscle pathology was studied in 7 of the 11 affected individuals, 1 of them at autopsy, and correlated closely with clinical involvement. Clinically unaffected muscles showed minimal change. Moderately affected muscles showed fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and rimmed vacuoles with basophilic rims. In severely involved muscles, the fibers had been replaced by fat and fibrous connective tissue. The inclusions were Congophilic and reacted with antibodies to desmin, beta-amyloid, and phosphorylated tau protein.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2012) defined the phenotype in 31 carriers of a TTN mutation from 3 families who had been followed for up to 31 years. Patients presented with weakness that was mainly distal, mainly proximal, or mainly respiratory. Age at onset was highly variable, ranging from early adulthood to a mild phenotype in advanced age. In nearly all patients, weakness began earlier and was more severe in the lower limbs. Seven patients had axial weakness. Respiratory function declined gradually over time, and no patient had cardiomyopathy. On muscle MRI in 21 affected individuals, 20 had the characteristic involvement of the semitendinosus, including 3 who were presymptomatic. The most frequent histopathologic findings were eosinophilic inclusions (inclusion bodies) and rimmed vacuoles, but pathology was nonspecific in a minority of patients.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2014) described 11 patients from 5 British families with the TTN C30071R mutation. Onset was typically in the fourth or fifth decade, with tripping, falling, myalgia, and difficulty walking. Creatine kinase ranged from normal to 1195 IU/L. The disease progressed slowly and involved proximal, distal, and axial muscles. Only 1 patient lost the ability to walk, after about 25 years. Pulmonary function was abnormal in 10 of 11 patients, indicating respiratory muscle weakness, and 4 required nocturnal noninvasive ventilation 20 to 30 years after onset. Features not previously noted included scapular winging, which was often asymmetric, contractures of the elbows and/or Achilles tendons, variable spinal rigidity, and muscle hypertrophy. Cardiac involvement was limited to mild left ventricular impairment in 1 patient and supraventricular tachycardia in 1. Muscle MRI in 3 patients, 1 of them presymptomatic, showed early involvement of the semitendinosus and peroneus longus muscles. Muscle biopsies showed myopathic or dystrophic changes. Rimmed vacuoles were present in 3 biopsies, and inclusions that were eosinophilic and dark blue on Gomori trichrome were present in 3. In 6 of 7 biopsies, desmin, myotilin, p62, and ubiquitin had accumulated in the cytoplasm. Three biopsies showed cytoplasmic aggregates with a 'cheetah skin' appearance, best seen with myotilin staining, and the inclusions did not fully overlap with the protein accumulations. The authors concluded that these features supported a diagnosis of myofibrillar myopathy.

paragraphs.text: Lange et al. (2005) identified a signaling complex in which the titin protein kinase domain (TK) interacts with the zinc finger protein nbr1 through a mechanically inducible conformation. Nbr1 targets the ubiquitin-associated protein p62/SQSTM1 to sarcomeres. p62 in turn interacts with MuRF2, a muscle-specific RING-B-box E3 ligase that binds the transactivation domain of serum response factor (SRF). Mechanical inactivity caused MuRF2 to move into the nucleus, which reduced nuclear SRF and repressed transcription. The authors suggested that the titin kinase domain controls muscle gene expression and protein turnover in response to mechanical load.

checks.claim: The probands of 5 new and 3 previously reported families with the TTN C30071R mutation shared a core haplotype of 171 kb.
checks.evidence_quote: Haplotype analysis indicated a shared region of 171 kbp between all 8 families with the p.C30071R mutation

checks.claim: The probability of the 171-kb core haplotype being shared by chance among TTN C30071R families was less than 10(-6).
checks.evidence_quote: the probability of this shared haplotype occurring in 8 unrelated families by chance is less than 10-6

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R mutation was concluded to be an ancient British founder mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: The very small size of the shared haplotype suggests an ancient mutation, or that (less likely) the mutation occurred more than once in time on similar haplotype backgrounds of approximately 171 kbp.
checks.explanation: The paper hedges. A British founder effect is called 'likely' and an ancient origin is only suggested, with recurrent mutation left open. It did not firmly conclude that this is an ancient British founder mutation.
